## Motivation

The Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) operates digit games and
jackpot games on recurring weekly schedules. Published results create a useful
teaching setting because the records combine dates, categorical game labels,
draw times, number strings, monetary values, and row-level source provenance.
Students can practice reshaping and validating semi-structured fields before
asking inferential questions about coverage, marginal number frequencies, or
sequential patterns.

This is an observational, independently compiled snapshot, **not an official
PCSO database**. It combines publicly reported draw facts for nine games. The
snapshot is fixed at version 2.0.1 so that classroom analyses are reproducible.
Most rows cite a secondary public results archive; the `source_url` field should
therefore remain attached to every row. Apparent gaps can reflect source
coverage, holidays, special schedule changes, or collection errors and should
not automatically be interpreted as cancelled draws.

Lottery draws are also a useful setting for discussing the limits of
statistical inference. Retrospective frequency or independence checks can
identify unusual patterns in this snapshot, but they cannot predict future
winning numbers or establish a problem with a draw process by themselves.

## Data

`philippines-pcso-draw-results-2022-2026.csv` contains 13,457 rows. Each row is
one published result for one game, date, and scheduled draw time. The snapshot
covers January 2, 2022 through July 20, 2026, though the exact first and last
dates differ by game. It contains 4,295 2D Lotto results, 4,296 3D Lotto
results, and between 676 and 705 results for each of seven other games.

There are no duplicate `(lottery_slug, draw_date, draw_time)` keys. All rows
have a non-empty winning-number string and source URL, and all have status
`published`. `jackpot_amount` is blank for 10,034 rows. This is expected for the
digit games and also occurs when a monetary value was unavailable in the cited
source. A blank amount must not be treated as zero. Currency is not encoded in
the file; monetary analysis should first verify values against the cited source
and document any assumptions.

The source distribution is itself an important limitation: 13,450 rows cite
`www.lottopcso.com`, six cite `philnews.ph`, and one cites `lottolensph.com`.
These counts describe provenance in this snapshot, not independent
confirmation of every row.

`philippines-pcso-draw-schedule.csv` contains nine rows, one per game. It records
the normal schedule and result format as a compact lookup table. Schedule data
describes the normal timetable; holidays and PCSO announcements can supersede
it.

### Draw-result variables

| Variable | Description |
|----|-------------|
| `lottery_slug` | Stable lowercase identifier for the game. |
| `draw_date` | Calendar date of the draw in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. |
| `draw_time` | Scheduled draw label, such as `2PM`, `5PM`, `9PM`, or `9PM Main`. |
| `winning_numbers` | Winning digits or balls stored as a hyphen-separated character string. Parse digit and jackpot games separately, preserving leading zeroes. |
| `jackpot_amount` | Reported jackpot amount when available; blank means unavailable or not applicable, not zero. Currency is not encoded and should be verified before monetary analysis. |
| `status` | Publication status. Every row in this fixed snapshot is `published`. |
| `published_at` | Timestamp at which the result was recorded, including UTC offset. This is not necessarily the official draw time. |
| `source_name` | Human-readable label for the cited public results source. |
| `source_url` | Row-level URL used as provenance for the reported result. |

### Schedule variables

| Variable | Description |
|----|-------------|
| `game_slug` | Stable lowercase identifier matching `lottery_slug` in the results file. |
| `game_name` | Display name of the lottery game. |
| `game_type` | `digit` or `jackpot`. |
| `result_format` | Expected number of digits or balls in a result. |
| `normal_draw_days` | Normal days on which draws are scheduled. |
| `normal_draw_times_pht` | Normal draw times in Philippine Time, separated by semicolons when more than one applies. |
| `timezone` | IANA time-zone identifier for the schedule (`Asia/Manila`). |
| `official_source` | Link to the official PCSO website. |
| `reference_page` | LottoLens PH game page documenting the schedule used in this snapshot. |

## Questions

1. Build an expected sequence of draw slots from the schedule table. For each
   game and month, compare expected and observed slots and visualize where
   coverage differs. Which discrepancies can be explained by holidays or
   special PCSO announcements, and which remain source-coverage questions?

2. Parse `winning_numbers`, treating digit games separately from jackpot games.
   For each game, compare marginal number frequencies with the distribution
   expected under a simple uniform model. Use chi-squared or Monte Carlo
   methods, report effect sizes, and account for multiple testing. How sensitive
   are conclusions to the chosen time window?

3. Test whether consecutive draws show more repeated digits or balls than
   simulated independent draws with the same game rules. What assumptions are
   required? Explain why a retrospective rejection or non-rejection does not
   provide a strategy for predicting the next result.

4. For rows with a verified monetary value, describe jackpot distributions by
   game and identify outliers. How do results change when the analysis excludes
   values whose units or source records cannot be independently confirmed? Do
   not treat blank amounts as zero.

5. Examine how source coverage changes over time. Are particular games, dates,
   or draw times associated with a change in `source_name` or a missing expected
   slot? Discuss why source selection and collection coverage limit any causal
   interpretation.
